# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about who can reach whom. I'm Mute: I can only gesture, and only Deaf receives my gestures. I cannot reach Blind at all directly. Blind is the one who acts, but Blind can only feel the bomb, not see gestures or hear speech. So I must pass information to Deaf, and Deaf must speak to Blind (Deaf can gesture but not hear/speak... wait let me check Deaf's abilities).

Deaf can see the bomb but cannot hear or speak. So Deaf cannot speak to Blind either. Let me reconsider: Blind cannot see gestures or printed things, and cannot hear? No - Blind's restriction is "cannot see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed." Blind can hear presumably, since only "cannot see" is listed. So Blind can hear speech.

So the chain: Mute (has manual) -> gestures -> Deaf (sees bomb, sees gestures) -> Deaf speaks -> Blind (hears, acts). Deaf needs to relay both the bomb's light color and my manual mapping to Blind via speech.

I need to encode the manual using gestures for Deaf. Let me use symbols to represent light colors and wire colors: e.g., 👍=blue, ✌=green, ☝=red for lights; and same or different symbols for wire colors. I'll define a simple gesture code.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Display shows 0. Light is red. Sign embossed says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Three wires: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

I need to respond, but wait - I'm Mute, I cannot speak, only gesture, and only Deaf can receive gestures (Blind can't see gestures). So I can't directly tell Blind anything. But Deaf just "said" something to me - but I can't hear! Let me re-check: Mute cannot hear. So that "Deaf says to Mute" text shouldn't actually reach me... but it's shown in my context as what arrived. Perhaps this is a system convenience showing me the transcript, but actually per rules, Mute cannot hear speech at all - "You cannot speak" is stated, but can Mute hear? Looking at the table: Mute "Cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb" - hearing isn't restricted for Mute! So Mute CAN hear. Good, that resolves it.

So Deaf spoke to me (Mute) - meaning Deaf can speak? Wait Deaf's cannot list: "Hear anything, or touch the bomb". Deaf cannot hear, but nothing says Deaf cannot speak. So Deaf can speak. Good, that makes sense - Deaf speaks, others who can hear (Mute, Blind) receive it.

So: Deaf saw red light, wires are green/yellow/blue. Per manual: red -> cut green wire. The embossed sign "DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE" is bomb's misleading print - manual says ignore bomb, trust manual only.

I need to tell Blind to cut the green wire. But I can't speak, and Blind can't see my gestures. I need to relay through Deaf... but Deaf already spoke this turn, and turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf - so my message now goes to Blind (next in this round) and Deaf (already passed, will get it next round).

Since Blind can hear speech but I cannot speak - I can only gesture, and Blind cannot see gestures. So I literally cannot communicate with Blind at all, ever, directly!

The only path: Mute -> gesture -> Deaf -> speak -> Blind. But timing: this round order is Mute, Blind, Deaf. If I gesture to Deaf now, Deaf gets it only next round (after Blind's turn this round). That's too late for this round's Blind turn, but Blind can wait this round.

I'll gesture the answer (cut green) to Deaf now, so Deaf can tell Blind next round.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌"])
```

Deaf says to Mute: I see your gesture repeated: point then two-fingers. Do you mean wire number 2 is the one to cut, or wire 2 is dangerous? Confirm with thumbs up for cut, thumbs down for danger.

Deaf is asking me to clarify my gesture using thumbs up/down. My gesture was ☝ (ONE - meant to signal "red" from my earlier code) then ✌ (meant "green" in my earlier code). But Deaf interpreted ☝ as "wire number 1" and ✌ as "wire number 2" - a completely different reading. I need to clear this up carefully.

Deaf already knows: light is red, wires are green/yellow/blue by color name (not number labels 1/2/3, though Deaf listed them as "1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue" - so wire 1=green, wire 2=yellow, wire 3=blue).

Per manual: red light → cut the GREEN wire. That's wire #1 in Deaf's numbering.

I need to signal clearly: cut wire 1 (green). Deaf offered a thumbs up/down protocol for confirming "wire 2." That doesn't match what I want. I should not confirm wire 2 - I need to redirect to wire 1.

Let me use a clean gesture scheme: point with ☝ to mean "wire one", and 👍 to confirm "cut this one".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
```
